occasions.recipeTitle: Pomegranate & Ras El Hanout Braised Lamb Shoulder
occasions.cuisine: Middle Eastern · North African · For Two · Scales to 12

swaps.text: butternut squash + chickpeas, same spices, roasted alongside the lamb

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Toss diced squash and drained chickpeas with the same spices as the lamb rub, plus a little oil. Spread on a separate tray.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Slide the tray into the same oven as the lamb, alongside the casserole, for the last 55 minutes of the braise — same shelf if there's room, otherwise the shelf below.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Straight from the oven, no rest needed. Finishes right as the lamb comes out.

swaps.text: salmon, half the ras el hanout, roasted after the lamb comes out

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Pat salmon fillets dry. Rub with half the ras el hanout — the milder spicing lets the fish stay the point, not the spice. Season with salt.

phases.name: Roast
phases.desc: Oven up once the lamb comes out. Roast salmon skin-side down on a lined tray until just cooked through and lightly flaking.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Straight from the oven — salmon doesn't rest like the lamb does. Plate alongside the same couscous, yogurt, and mint.

swaps.text: plain chicken thighs, separate pan, mild braising liquid

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Season chicken thighs plainly — salt and pepper only, no ras el hanout. Keep it separate from the spiced braising liquid.

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown thighs in their own pan on the stovetop while the lamb is still braising.

phases.name: Simmer
phases.desc: Add a ladle of the lamb's braising liquid (strained, no whole spices) to keep it mild. Cover, simmer until cooked through.

phases.name: Cook the orzo
phases.desc: In a separate pot, cook the orzo in salted water, or in a second ladle of the same strained braising liquid for extra flavor without the spice. Drain if using water.

phases.name: Rest
phases.desc: Chicken off the heat, loosely covered.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Chicken over the orzo, both moistened with a little extra braising liquid if needed.

phases.name: Prep
phases.desc: Score the lamb deeply all over. Rub entirely with ras el hanout, olive oil and a generous amount of salt. Let the spice crust set before searing.

phases.name: Sear
phases.desc: Brown all sides in a heavy casserole over high heat until a deep mahogany crust forms. This is where the flavour lives — don't rush it.

phases.name: Braise
phases.desc: Add aromatics, stock and braising liquid. Cover tight. The house will fill with something extraordinary.

phases.name: Rest
phases.desc: Out of the oven, uncovered. Skim the fat from the braising liquid. Shred coarsely back into the juices with two forks.

phases.name: Serve
phases.desc: Over couscous with cold Greek yogurt, fresh mint, and pomegranate seeds scattered at the last moment. Serve family-style.

pairings: Bold Moroccan Syrah or Côtes du Rhône
